nodes.label: google-ecosystem repo for connecting a Google account via official CLI
nodes.norm_label: google ecosystem repo for connecting a google account via official cli
nodes.summary: The session's subject. A repo at ~/Proyek/google-ecosystem (renamed from Google-ekosistem at the user's request) holding prerequisites, token locations, the two auth modes, a read-only scripts/cek-cli.sh diagnostic, and notes/. The stated purpose is connecting the user's Google account using officially sanctioned CLI tooling and Google Cloud Console authentication.

nodes.label: gcloud's default token scope does not reach Gmail or Drive
nodes.norm_label: gclouds default token scope does not reach gmail or drive
nodes.summary: Measured, not assumed: the gcloud access token carries only cloud-platform, and calls to gmail.googleapis.com and drive.googleapis.com both returned 403 insufficient authentication scopes. gcloud also rejects --scopes=.../auth/drive with invalid_scope. The conclusion recorded is that gcloud is not a tool for Gmail or Drive — those CLIs hold their own OAuth clients and their own token stores.

nodes.label: Admin SDK can be enabled without Workspace but cannot be used
nodes.norm_label: admin sdk can be enabled without workspace but cannot be used
nodes.summary: gcloud services enable admin.googleapis.com succeeds and is free — Cloud does not check the subscription. What fails is use: gcloud's scope allowlist has no admin.directory.* scope at all (rejecting admin.directory.user.readonly with Invalid scopes value), and GET /admin/directory/v1/users?customer=my_customer returns HTTP 400 Invalid Input while /customer/my_customer returns 404, because the Directory API needs a customer domain and a super-admin role that a consumer @gmail.com account has neither of. Admin SDK was struck from the repo's requirements.

nodes.label: The AUR gdrive package is a third-party Rust rewrite, not prasmussen's and not Google's
nodes.norm_label: the aur gdrive package is a third party rust rewrite not prasmussens and not googles
nodes.summary: A correction made twice in the session: the AUR gdrive package pulls glotlabs/gdrive (MIT, ~2.1k stars), a Rust rewrite of the old gdrive2, not prasmussen/gdrive as the README first claimed. Google has never published a Drive CLI of its own, so the user's target of an 'official Google CLI' does not exist for Drive; only gcloud is official and it does not touch the Drive API.

nodes.label: rclone from the Arch extra repo as the Drive client
nodes.norm_label: rclone from the arch extra repo as the drive client
nodes.summary: rclone 1.75.1 from Arch extra, signed by packager T.J. Townsend, 109 MiB installed, config at ~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf mode 600. It became the Drive path for the repo after gdrive was assessed as a supply-chain risk, and it is what the later half of the session (listing, searching, moving, reorganising) actually operates through.

nodes.label: For a Desktop-app OAuth client the secret is not a secret; the refresh token is
nodes.norm_label: for a desktop app oauth client the secret is not a secret the refresh token is
nodes.summary: Checked against Google's documentation rather than asserted: for the Desktop-app client type Google states the client secret is 'obviously not treated as a secret', so the Client ID should be treated as a public identifier. The genuinely sensitive artefact is the refresh token in ~/.config/gdrive3/. Two consequences recorded: deleting the client in the console kills every token issued under it (recoverable for 30 days, permanent after), and there is a limit of 100 refresh tokens per account per client ID, at which point the oldest are cancelled without warning.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-10-01 - inisiasi-folder-proyek-google-ekosistem [ses_f0aa41cdfffe58eSx30xIomnBi].md:L6424] Using your own OAuth client is safer because you hold the revocation

nodes.label: Consent screen in Testing status silently expires refresh tokens in 7 days
nodes.norm_label: consent screen in testing status silently expires refresh tokens in 7 days
nodes.summary: One of two timing traps recorded in the notes: a consent screen left in Testing status issues refresh tokens that expire after 7 days with no notification, so the status must be set to In production. The companion trap is an OAuth client idle for 6 months, which Google auto-deletes with a warning email 30 days beforehand.

nodes.label: IAP OAuth Admin API shutdown makes OAuth-client creation impossible from the CLI
nodes.norm_label: iap oauth admin api shutdown makes oauth client creation impossible from the cli
nodes.summary: The one remaining CLI path, gcloud iap oauth-clients create, reports from gcloud itself: 'March 19, 2026: The IAP OAuth Admin APIs will be permanently shut down.' No other API covers OAuth-client creation, and Google's own docs for gcloud auth application-default login now point back to the web console. Creating the Desktop-app client is therefore a manual browser step, and the session documents that as a hard requirement rather than working around it.

nodes.label: OAuth client of type Desktop app, created in the Google Auth Platform console
nodes.norm_label: oauth client of type desktop app created in the google auth platform console
nodes.summary: The concrete artefact the whole Drive effort depends on: Google Auth Platform -> Clients -> Create client -> Desktop app, consent screen External with three mandatory fields, publishing status In production, and at minimum the drive.file scope. Its downloaded JSON has a top-level 'installed' key; a second file in ~/Unduhan had a top-level 'web' key and was flagged as an unplanned leftover client. One unexplained checkbox, 'This client will be used by an AI-powered agent', had no official documentation and was left as the user's decision.

nodes.label: drive.file scope versus the restricted full drive scope
nodes.norm_label: drive file scope versus the restricted full drive scope
nodes.summary: The central access decision. drive.file is non-sensitive and grants only the files the user picks at login; the full drive scope is restricted and requires restricted-scope verification plus a security assessment if the token is ever stored on a server. The session started narrow, which immediately became a problem: with drive.file a search for 'Beasiswa' returned zero results while the file did exist, and the user was visibly angry about it before the scope was widened to full drive.

nodes.label: An empty result under a narrow scope is not evidence of absence
nodes.norm_label: an empty result under a narrow scope is not evidence of absence
nodes.summary: The lesson the session writes down about itself: with the initial drive.file remote, searching for Beasiswa returned nothing and the assistant initially reported that as a finding. The positive control settled it — the same filter with correct syntax returned empty while the unfiltered listing returned 3 files, proving the method worked and the scope, not the query, was limiting. Recorded as: distinguish 'not found' under a narrow scope from 'does not exist' before concluding.

nodes.label: rclone moveto is a server-side rename that preserves the file ID
nodes.norm_label: rclone moveto is a server side rename that preserves the file id
nodes.summary: The mechanism that made bulk reorganisation reversible: moveto is a rename on Google's side, so the file ID does not change and existing share links keep working, and moving a file back is one command with no re-download. Chosen over copy+delete, which would detach large files from the drive in the interim. The session also records the limit: moving breaks folder-level sharing and Google Docs shortcuts pointing at the old location.

nodes.label: Bulk Drive reorganisation is surveyed and planned before anything moves
nodes.norm_label: bulk drive reorganisation is surveyed and planned before anything moves
nodes.summary: Asked to reorganise 3000+ files with a free hand on new folders, the session stopped and refused to start, for three recorded reasons: what counts as 'messy' could not be confirmed (the 3029 files were already nested in tidy emoji-prefixed folders), moving breaks other people's links and Docs shortcuts, and unlimited discretion over new categories means guessing — and a wrong guess is hard to unpick at hundreds of files. After an inventory of root (74 entries: 38 files, 36 folders) a three-folder plan was proposed and approved before any move.

nodes.label: Drive files classified by extracted content, not by filename
nodes.norm_label: drive files classified by extracted content not by filename
nodes.summary: After the user pointed out that titles were being trusted instead of the files, all 19 remaining files were opened — text extraction for docx/pdf/eml, direct viewing for images and video — and 15 moved. Four findings changed decisions: a deck named for Accounting actually contained Sistem Informasi material; a WhatsApp image was three lecture slides from Universitas Wijaya Mukti; a WhatsApp video was a screen recording of Snipset 9.1.0; and a deck assumed unreadable turned out to be a BCA Divisi Cash Management deck once ppt/media was extracted. Filenames and MIME types were treated as untrustworthy labels throughout.
